topics.title: Binomial Distribution
topics.summary: A discrete probability distribution representing the number of successes in a fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials.

topics.title: Point Estimation for Proportions
topics.summary: The process of finding a single value (estimate) or a rule (estimator) to represent the true population proportion p.

topics.title: Method of Moments (MM)
topics.summary: An estimation technique that equates the sample mean to the theoretical expected value of the distribution to solve for parameters.

topics.title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE)
topics.summary: A method of estimating parameters by maximizing the likelihood function, often using the log-likelihood for mathematical simplicity.

topics.title: Confidence Intervals for Proportions
topics.summary: Statistical ranges used to estimate the true population proportion with a specific level of confidence.

topics.title: Wald Confidence Interval
topics.summary: A confidence interval based on the Gaussian (Normal) approximation of the binomial distribution, typically using the standard error.

topics.title: Wilson Score Interval
topics.summary: An alternative confidence interval for proportions that provides better coverage than the Wald interval, especially for small samples or extreme proportions.

topics.title: Exact Confidence Interval
topics.summary: A confidence interval derived directly from the binomial distribution (e.g., Clopper-Pearson) rather than a normal approximation.

topics.title: Hypothesis Testing for Proportions
topics.summary: Statistical procedures used to test claims about a single proportion or the difference between two proportions.

topics.title: Chi-squared Test of Independence
topics.summary: A test used to determine if there is a significant association between two categorical variables in a contingency table.

topics.title: Fisher's Exact Test
topics.summary: A statistical significance test used in the analysis of contingency tables, particularly useful for small sample sizes where Chi-squared assumptions fail.

topics.title: Continuity Correction
topics.summary: An adjustment applied when a continuous distribution (like the Normal) is used to approximate a discrete distribution (like the Binomial).

topics.title: Relative Risk (RR)
topics.summary: The ratio of the probability of an outcome in an exposed group to the probability of an outcome in an unexposed group.

topics.title: Odds Ratio (OR)
topics.summary: A measure of association between an exposure and an outcome, representing the odds that an outcome will occur given a particular exposure compared to the odds in the absence of that exposure.
